bull.b: Record leasing activity and a large booked-not-billed backlog provide multi-year revenue visibility and support continued growth without relying solely on new customer wins. This strengthens planning, improves development confidence, and supports management’s expectation for sustained FFO growth through 2027 and beyond.

High occupancy, record-low churn, and strong renewal spreads indicate durable customer retention and pricing power across the portfolio. These conditions support same-capital NOI growth, improve the economics of expiring leases, and provide an ongoing internal driver of recurring earnings.

Demand is broadening from large training deployments into enterprise AI, inference, sovereign workloads, and connectivity-rich environments. This expands the addressable customer base for Digital Realty’s global platform and reinforces structural demand for colocation, interconnection, and specialized infrastructure.

bear.b: Growing scrutiny over power, water, emissions, noise, and local community impacts can make approvals and grid access more difficult. These constraints may lengthen project timelines, restrict expansion in attractive markets, and increase the operational and capital required to deliver future capacity.

bear.t: High development intensity and cost pressure
bear.b: Digital Realty’s growth plan requires substantial development spending, while industry delays, inflation, customer-requested rework, and power constraints can pressure project returns. A large construction pipeline therefore creates execution risk and may defer the timing of revenue and cash-flow realization.

Although recent cash generation improved, the multi-year record shows volatile profitability and cash conversion, with unusually low TTM gross margin and prior negative free cash flow. This variability can reduce funding flexibility and make reported earnings less consistently translate into distributable cash.
